strings.name: Abdulrazak Gurnah
strings.role: Novelist and scholar · Colonial history and displacement
strings.summary: Raised in Zanzibar, Gurnah moved to Britain as a young man. His English-language novels explore the Indian Ocean world, colonial rule and complicated belonging after migration. Paradise, By the Sea and Afterlives place historical forces within ordinary relationships and choices, resisting simple accounts of refugee identity. He also studies postcolonial literature. The 2021 Nobel laureate continued examining inequality and young lives in Theft in 2025.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1948–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Addressed colonial history, exile and identity in novels including Paradise, broadening the expression of East African experience in international English-language literature.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Histories of the Indian Ocean world
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Paradise and Afterlives connect East African lives with colonial expansion, bringing overlooked relationships and memories into view.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Complex belonging after migration
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: By the Sea and other works examine refugees’ stories, silences and misunderstandings across histories and languages.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses Berlin’s colonial past
strings.timeline.event-01.text: In a HEIST interview he discussed museums, human remains and East African history, including historical sources behind Afterlives.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Publishes Theft
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The novel follows intersecting young lives in Tanzania, examining class, intimacy and unequal opportunities after his Nobel recognition.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Receives the Nobel Prize in Literature
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The Swedish Academy recognized his writing on colonialism and refugees, prompting broader reading of his accumulated work.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Publishes Afterlives
strings.timeline.event-04.text: East African lives reveal German colonial rule and its aftermath, connecting war and labor with family relationships.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Publishes By the Sea
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Two men from Zanzibar encounter each other in Britain, confronting histories of property, kinship and competing accounts of the past.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Publishes Paradise
strings.timeline.event-06.text: A young man’s journey through East Africa examines commerce, enslavement and colonial power; the novel reached the Booker shortlist.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Publishes his first novel
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Memory of Departure began a sustained fictional career with a young person’s departure from home and frustrated hopes.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Completes his doctorate at Kent
strings.timeline.event-08.text: His research on criticism of West African fiction preceded a career combining teaching, scholarship and novel-writing.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Moves to Britain
strings.timeline.event-09.text: He left Zanzibar for Britain; migration, unfamiliar languages and colonial history became recurring concerns in his fiction.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Zanzibar
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born and raised on Zanzibar, whose multilingual society and maritime connections later informed his literary imagination.
